subject: Decision constraints and approval path — next steps and owners
message_1_subject: Decision constraints and approval path — next steps and owners
message_1_body:
Thanks again for a productive call today — quick recap and proposed next steps below.

High-level decision criteria we captured today:
- Latency: target p95 inference latency <= 300ms for typical 1–2k token generative calls (external SLO goal).
- Cost: target blended unit economics < $0.02 per inference (average expected), with an annualized spend band to justify Dedicated reservation.
- Hosting preference: primary preference is VPC / Private deployment (PHI concerns) but open to a Dedicated-hosted lane if BAA + VPC peering are available.
- SLA: uptime target 99.9% with a clear credit policy for degradations; P95 latency SLOs for production routes.

Security & procurement gates mentioned:
1) SOC 2 Type II evidence and HIPAA BAA — required before pilot contains PHI.
2) Customer-managed KMS or HSM for keying (preferred).
3) Network: VPC peering or private link; audit logs retention 1 year min.
4) Standard security questionnaire (we can pre-fill common sections).

Immediate ask / next steps I own: 
- Attached: 'decision_matrix_celerity_v1.xlsx' with a simple table to map criteria to owners and pass/fail thresholds (please scan and flag missing rows).
- Karthik and Neha will produce a short note on hosting options (tradeoffs: Dedicated vs Private) and expected performance numbers for your 512–2k token profile by EOD tomorrow.
- Jordan will follow up on commercial cadence / seat counts in case the CFO wants an ARR projection.

Requested owners on your side (please confirm):
- Economic buyer / CFO: Alex Summers (confirm)?
- Procurement lead: Monica Ruiz (Monica — are you the right procurement contact or should we loop someone else?)
- Security reviewer: do you have a named security lead we should engage for SOC2/architecture review?

Proposed timeline: procurement + security review (2 weeks), pilot (1 month), exec review for committed capacity (week of Sep 13). Happy to compress if you want to run with a smaller pilot first.

Attachments: decision_matrix_celerity_v1.xlsx (matrix), redwood-sla-summary.pdf (SLA + credit policy draft).

Thanks — will stand up a shared Drive doc and calendar invite when owners are confirmed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

message_2_body:

- Confirmed ownership: I (Alex Summers) will be the economic buyer and will own the final approval on spend.
- Procurement contact: looping in Monica Ruiz (procurement) — Monica, can you confirm our standard PO/contract process and estimated lead time for vendor onboarding?
- Security lead: Lydia will coordinate with our security architect; I'll share the contact tomorrow.

On requirements: the latency target you listed aligns with our expectations for user-facing inference; cost target looks reasonable but we need clearer run-rate bands (e.g., low/med/high usage buckets). Can you share a short pricing/consumption example for pilot vs committed capacity?

Also please confirm whether Redwood would be willing to provide a data handling addendum for PHI during the pilot (we need that to start ingesting test data).

On quoting SLA: we need a draft that specifies uptime credit tiers and a P95 latency SLO for the production route. If you can share the 'redwood-sla-summary.pdf' (attached) with the credit language we can have our legal review parallel to procurement.

Looking forward — thanks for the template.

—Alex

message_3_subject: Re: Decision constraints and approval path — next steps and owners
message_3_body:
Alex — thanks for confirming. Quick answers and next deliverables: 

1) Pricing bands: attaching a simple run-rate sketch inside the decision matrix (low / med / high). For context: pilot (low) assumes up to 200k tokens/day; committed (med) assumes 1–2M tokens/day. We’ll convert to an ARR estimate for Jordan to include in the analysis.

2) PHI addendum / BAA: we can provide a BAA for the pilot; Neha will coordinate required scoping for data flows and redaction recommendations.

3) Hosting tradeoffs (high-level):
   - Private (VPC) — best for PHI and network isolation; higher setup time (1–3 weeks depending on networking); supports CMK.
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed, reserved capacity) — faster onboarding, predictable throughput; can be configured for private peering in many cases but requires additional legal/ops steps for PHI.
   - Hosted (multi-tenant) — fastest but not recommended for PHI.

4) SLA / credits: attached draft 'redwood-sla-summary.pdf' — it includes 99.9% uptime tiers and an example credit schedule. Please flag any must-have contract language (e.g., specific data destruction timelines, audit support windows).

Proposed next meetings: 
- Procurement Q&A (Monica + Jordan + our legal): 30m this week — Jordan, Marissa: can you pick 2 slots?
- Technical onboarding sync (Karthik + Neha + Lydia's security lead): 45m early next week.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: send calendar options and populate Drive sheet (today) — DONE (link above).
- Karthik: short doc on expected p95/p99 numbers under Dedicated vs Private (tomorrow EOD).
- Neha: BAA / pilot scoping checklist (EOD tomorrow).
- Jordan: draft ARR projection example (Tue).

If that reads right I’ll send invites and drop the matrix into shared Drive.

Best,
Marissa
